parts.label: Part 1
parts.article:
Part one. You will hear a man phoning a friend to ask for advice about an upcoming trip. First, you have some time to look at questions one to four.

Now listen carefully and answer questions one to four.

Hello?

Hi, Suzy. It's Steve.

Steve, hi. How are you doing?

I'm fine, thanks. Actually, I've got to attend a conference in July in Tucson, Arizona, and I was hoping you could give me a few tips. You're from around there, aren't you?

I sure am. Tucson's not my hometown, though, but it's definitely worth seeing.

[chuckles] What's the weather like around then? Is it true it's about forty degrees centigrade in the daytime?

That's right. And not less than twenty-five at night. A bit different from England in July.

[laughs] True. I was wondering what to take with me. I won't need warm clothes then, will I? [chuckles]

Well, you'll find that everywhere is air-conditioned, and it can feel quite cold sometimes, so a jacket would be a good idea.

You might need an umbrella as well, as we sometimes have thunderstorms during the day, but you can always pick one up when you get there.

My conference is only for a couple of days, so I was wondering what I could do in Tucson.

Well, it's a beautiful position. I'd hire a car in Tucson and then follow the trails in the desert.

Okay. I'm writing all this down. Uh, any other tips? Museums and stuff?

Well, there are lots of museums. The usual thing, like wildlife and history. But I think the most interesting is the space museum, so my advice would be to go there.

Hmm, what else? Well, there are plenty of walks you can do. The town itself is great, and there are plenty of places you can eat and drink when you get too hot and tired.

Any chance of a game of golf?

Oh, absolutely. There are loads of courses around Tucson.

Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions five to ten on page two.

Now listen and answer questions five to ten.

If you've got time, why don't you visit my parents? They'd love to see you.

Great. Uh, can you give me their address?

Sure. They live in the town of Williams at six-zero-seven-three Fearnleigh Drive.

Okay. Uh, how do you spell that?

F-E-A-R-N-L-E-I-G-H.

Six-zero-seven-three Fearnleigh Drive.

Okay, got that.

The town's in northern Arizona, and it's named after a hunter in the area in the early eighteen hundreds. He used to make a living shooting animals around there for their skins.

Hmm, sounds interesting. So is it full of old buildings?

Well, the post office is the oldest, as it was built in eighteen eighty-one, but there was a big fire in nineteen oh one, and most of the town was burnt down.

But it didn't take them long to rebuild. Oh, and the famous Route sixty-six goes through the town. That was built in nineteen twenty-six.

So when exactly are you going?

The conference is from the first to the second of July. Will your parents be at home after that?

Oh, yes. They wouldn't miss the Fourth of July, Independence Day.

Ah, [chuckles] okay. So lots of fireworks?

As soon as the sun goes down. People come from miles around to see them.

Why don't you give my parents a call? They're on nine-two-eight-six-three-five-double two-seven-one. I'm sure they'd love to have you.

[chuckles] Okay. I'll do that tonight.

And really, you shouldn't be in Arizona without taking a trip to the Grand Canyon for a few days. Hold on, I-I've got a leaflet here.

I took a friend there last summer. She had a great time.

Okay, it says here that there are a lot of tours you can take when you get there.

Someone told me you could take a helicopter. Can I do that?

Sure. That tour takes about one and a half hours, and there are seven a day to choose from. The last is five thirty. You get a really good idea of the huge size of the canyon from up there.

Sounds good. Any chance I can get down to the river? I'm quite good in a canoe. [chuckles]

[chuckles] Yes, you can do that too. Uh, let's see. Ah, yes, there's an all-day trip. They provide you with waterproof clothes, but they recommend you bring sun cream. You'll really need it down on the river.

Well, that should keep me busy for a few days. Oh, thanks, Suzy. That's terrific. I'll ring you again just before I go...

That is the end of Section One. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

analyses.content: 男士提问带什么物品，女士解释因为室内空调冷，所以建议带 jacket（外套）。
你可能会因为听到 warm clothes 或 umbrella 就直接填，但前者是男士预判不需要的，后者是女士随后补充且可以现买的，最核心的携带建议是 jacket。

I was wondering what to take with me. I won't need warm clothes then, will I? [chuckles] Well, you'll find that everywhere is air-conditioned, and it can feel quite cold sometimes, so a jacket would be a good idea.
男士问在图森市能做什么，女士建议租车并沿着 desert（沙漠）里的 trails（小径）去开。
你可能会光顾着听交通工具（car），而忽略了题目问的是 trails 的具体位置，注意听 follow the trails 后面的介词短语补充。
My conference is only for a couple of days, so I was wondering what I could do in Tucson. Well, it's a beautiful position. I'd hire a car in Tucson and then follow the trails in the desert.
女士在列举了几个博物馆后，用最高级 the most interesting（对应题目 highly recommended）引出了真正推荐的 space museum。
你可能听到 wildlife 或 history 就急着填，但女士用 but 进行了转折，排除了这两个常规选项。
Museums and stuff? Well, there are lots of museums. The usual thing, like wildlife and history. But I think the most interesting is the space museum, so my advice would be to go there.
男士主动提问是否有机会打 golf（高尔夫），女士给出肯定答复并补充周围有很多球场。
你可能会把后面补充的 courses（球场）当作答案填进去，但结合题目“playing（玩/打）”的语境，这里填具体的运动项目 golf 才是合乎逻辑的。
Any chance of a game of golf? Oh, absolutely. There are loads of courses around Tucson.
女士直接报出了街道数字和名称，并在男士的请求下对 Fearnleigh 进行了逐字母拼读。
你可能会在拼写时漏掉中间不发音的 n 或者把 e 和 i 的顺序弄反，听到逐个字母拼读时一定要专注并迅速写下。

Uh, can you give me their address? Sure. They live in the town of Williams at six-zero-seven-three Fearnleigh Drive. Okay. Uh, how do you spell that? F-E-A-R-N-L-E-I-G-H. Six-zero-seven-three Fearnleigh Drive.
女士提到在这个小镇上，1901 年发生了一场 big fire（对应题目 destroyed by fire），大部分建筑被烧毁。
你可能会听到 1881（邮局建造年份）或者录音后文的 1926（66号公路建造年份）就直接填，但只有 1901 是紧跟着 fire 这个核心破坏事件的。

So is it full of old buildings? Well, the post office is the oldest, as it was built in eighteen eighty-one, but there was a big fire in nineteen oh one, and most of the town was burnt down. But it didn't take them long to rebuild.
男士询问是不是有 fireworks（烟花），女士给予确认并说明太阳一落山就开始。
题目问的是 in the evening（晚上的活动），你可能会干等 evening 这个词，但录音中用 as soon as the sun goes down 替换了晚上，确认了烟花这个活动。
So lots of fireworks? As soon as the sun goes down. People come from miles around to see them.
女士在建议男士打电话后，直接匀速报出了父母的一长串电话号码。
你可能会在听到 double two 的时候反应慢半拍只写了一个 2，连续报数字时必须对 double/triple 这类词保持极高的敏感度。
Why don't you give my parents a call? They're on nine-two-eight-six-three-five-double two-seven-one.
男士提出可以通过 helicopter（直升机）去游览，女士给予肯定，并补充了具体的时长（1.5小时）和班次（一天7趟）。
你可能会被录音前面的 tours 吸引注意力，但题目通过 by 明确需要一种具体的交通方式，抓住男士提问中的核心名词即可。
Someone told me you could take a helicopter. Can I do that? Sure. That tour takes about one and a half hours, and there are seven a day to choose from.
女士在介绍独木舟（canoe）全天行程时，明确指出官方建议游客自己携带（recommend you bring 对应题目 take）sun cream（防晒霜）。
你可能会一听到 waterproof clothes 就直接写上，但那是官方 provide（提供）的，题目问的是需要你自己 take（带）的物品。

Any chance I can get down to the river? I'm quite good in a canoe. [chuckles] [chuckles] Yes, you can do that too. Uh, let's see. Ah, yes, there's an all-day trip. They provide you with waterproof clothes, but they recommend you bring sun cream. You'll really need it down on the river.
